newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Russian ADRs fall on Yeltsin news.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Russian ADRs fall on Yeltsin news.

text.p: Russian shares fell in moderate U.S. trade on Thursday but avoided a steep sell-off after news that President Boris Yeltsin had agreed to undergo heart surgery.
"None of the international clients were sellers on the back of this," said Priscilla Coker, president at Brunswick Securities here.
"People are concerned. But everybody has known for some time that Yeltsin has not been well. I don't think it's any great surprise that he needs a heart operation," she added.
However, shares in Moscow were expected to come under more pressure due to uncertainty surrounding Yeltsin's operation, which is planned for the end of the month.
"We expect the market there to open down tomorrow, something like five to seven percent lower," Coker said.
Among Russian American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), LUKoil was indicated at 38 bid, 39 ask in afternoon trade after opening at 39 bid, 40 ask.
The indicated quote on Mosenergo was about 28-1/2 bid, 29-1/2 ask, versus its open at 30-1/2 bid, 31-1/2 ask.
GUM was at 35-1/8 bid, 39-1/8 ask, compared to its opening level of 34-1/2 bid, 38-1/2 ask.
Latin American ADRs were little changed, weighed down by the Dow ahead of Friday's U.S. August jobs data, which should give the market an indication of whether the Fed will raise interest rates.
"It's been absolutely dead quiet," one trader said. "People are waiting for tomorrow's (jobs) number to come out. Nobody wants to take a stand."
Mexico's Telmex slid 1/4 to 33-1/8, Brazil's Telebras lost 1/2 to 73-7/8, and Chile's CTC was up 3/4 at 98-3/4.
